subject: Post-call: deployment mode & cost sensitivity interlock
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@arborhealth.com>, Leah Summers <l.summers@arborhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment mode & cost sensitivity interlock

Hi Daniel / Leah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the deployment mode economics (hosted API vs dedicated capacity vs private VPC/on-prem):

Summary of buyer needs (as we understood on the call):
- Primary use: clinical summarization + patient triage model; 150k tokens/day average, peaks to ~600k tokens/day for batch tasks.
- Latency requirement: <200ms P95 for triage endpoint (human-in-the-loop) and best-effort for asynchronous batch jobs.
- Data controls: PHI cannot leave a controlled VPC for regulatory review; procurement evaluating private deployment but team wants cost comparison.
- Timeline: pilot in Q3, production roll by Q4 if economics and security checks align.

Action items we agreed:
1) Redwood to send a short TCO sketch showing: per-token hosted estimate, reserved committed cost for Dedicated (monthly commit tiers), and an indicative private/VPC on-prem estimate with one-time infra + recurring support (attach quick-sheet).
2) ArborHealth to share an anonymized weekly token distribution (sample week) and a short list of latency-sensitive endpoints so we can size Dedicated pools and quantify batching gains.
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement interlock (Leah + procurement) to confirm contract timelines and required compliance artifacts (SOC2, data flow diagram).

What Im attaching: a compact TCO workbook (ArborHealth_Quick_TCO_Scenarios.xlsx) with three scenarios: hosted-heavy, dedicated-commit, private-onprem (high-level assumptions). Its intentionally simple so we can iterate.

Next suggested date for pricing review + interlock: Wed 2 Jul or Thu 3 Jul, 10:00-11:00 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Irene, Marcus —

Thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- We can produce the token sample by EOD tomorrow (anonymized logs).
- Procurement would like to see both committed monthly pricing and a best-effort hosted capex-equivalent so we can compare to our internal run-rate.
- Private/on-prem: primary concern is the initial infra OPEX for our cloud team and the timeline for HIPA/PHI sign-off.

Leah, can you confirm availability for the procurement interlock on Thu 3 Jul 10am PT? If procurement needs a separate invite, loop them in.

Also a note on the latency bar: for the triage endpoint wed accept a short GRPC warm-up for sustained bursts if that materially reduces cost (i.e., batching allowed) but we cannot tolerate cold-start >500ms.

-Dan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-call: deployment mode & cost sensitivity interlock (internal calc)

Internal note (putting some quick math on the workbook before the call):

I ran three high-level scenarios using the sample assumptions in the attached workbook:
- Hosted API baseline: $0.0006 / input-token + $0.0008 / output-token (avg prompt: 300 tokens). For ArborHealth steady-state this maps to ~$9k/month for 150k tokens/day and ~$36k/month at 600k peak day distribution accounting.
- Dedicated (reserved commit): pricing sketches at commit tiers 300k, 600k, 1.2M tokens/day equivalent (this maps to reserved GPU pools). At ~600k/day steady the committed model looks ~35-45% cheaper than hosted per-token due to continuous batching and KV cache reuse; however, committed costs require a 12-month minimum and a 25% upfront reservation.
- Private / on-prem: one-time infra + integration ~ $120k-$180k (depends on customer infra agreements) + recurring support ~ $6k/month. For customers with sustained >800k tokens/day and strict PHI requirements, private becomes comparable after ~9-12 months when amortized.

Risks / notes to flag on the call:
- If they have high variance with unpredictable spikes, hosted protects them from commit overage but could be materially more expensive.
- If triage endpoint latency requirement forces small batch sizes, the realized savings on Dedicated drop to ~15-20% vs hosted. We should capture their P95 actuals during the pilot.

I added a second tab with a simple sensitivity chart (batch size vs % savings) and included the assumptions. Im happy to run a more granular per-model GPU hour calc if they provide model size and average sequence length.

-Rishi

Daniel / Leah / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the logs. Ive attached a short, redlined proposal (Proposal_ArborHealth_Q3.pdf) and the TCO workbook updated with Rishis sensitivity notes. High level asks before the procurement interlock: 

1) Please confirm the anonymized token sample is uploaded to the shared folder (or paste a short sample in-reply) so we can finalize sizing.
2) Confirm whether your security team requires HSM/KMS integration (we support both; if yes, well add the HSM add-on to the private estimate).
3) Procurement: can you share preferred contract term (12 vs 24 months) and whether you need a standalone SOW for Dedicated capacity?

Weve also prepared two optional paths for the pilot: a hosted trial with usage caps (fastest) OR a time-limited Dedicated pilot (30 days reserved capacity with a credit toward commit if they convert). The draft proposal includes both options with clear conversion mechanics.

If Thu 3 Jul 10:00am PT still works, Ill send a calendar invite with a short agenda and a concise slide with the commit math so procurement has something to review in advance.
